narration.en: A frog breathes through its skin under water and through its lungs on land, has a three-chambered heart, and its male gametes reach the cloaca through its kidneys. Let us open up its organ systems.

body.en: The alimentary canal is short because frogs are carnivores. The bilobed tip of the tongue captures prey. Food is digested in the stomach by HCl and gastric juices, and the partly digested chyme passes to the duodenum, which receives bile and pancreatic juice through a common bile duct. Digested food is absorbed by the villi and microvilli of the intestine. In water, the frog breathes through its moist skin (cutaneous respiration); on land, the buccal cavity, skin and lungs are used. During aestivation and hibernation, gas exchange is through the skin.
body.kn: ಕಪ್ಪೆ ಮಾಂಸಾಹಾರಿ, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಕರುಳು ಚಿಕ್ಕದು. ದ್ವಿಹಾಲೆಯ ನಾಲಿಗೆ ಬೇಟೆ ಹಿಡಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ನೀರಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಚರ್ಮದ ಮೂಲಕ ಉಸಿರಾಟ; ನೆಲದ ಮೇಲೆ ಬಾಯಿಯ ಕುಹರ, ಚರ್ಮ ಮತ್ತು ಶ್ವಾಸಕೋಶಗಳು.

narration.en: In water a frog breathes through its moist skin (cutaneous respiration). On land the buccal cavity, the skin and the lungs all work, and the lungs take most of the load. During hibernation and aestivation it breathes through the skin alone. A frog is cold-blooded, so warmer water raises its oxygen need.

say.en: The frog heart has three chambers: two atria and one ventricle.
The sinus venosus joins the right atrium; the ventricle opens into the conus arteriosus.
Circulation is closed, and the red blood cells have nuclei.
In water the frog breathes through its skin; on land also through the buccal cavity and lungs.
The kidneys remove urea, so the frog is ureotelic. All ducts open into the cloaca.

text.en: Moist skin, used for breathing in water
Buccal cavity in breathing on land
Three-chambered heart: two atria and one ventricle
Hepatic portal and renal portal systems
A pair of dark red, bean-like kidneys

explanation.en: The frog breathes through its skin in water and with lungs on land, has a three-chambered heart and excretes urea through its kidneys. The alimentary canal, ureters and reproductive ducts open into a common cloaca.

body.en: The frog has a closed circulatory system and a lymphatic system. The heart has three chambers, two atria and one ventricle, covered by a pericardium. A triangular sinus venosus joins the right atrium, and the ventricle opens into the conus arteriosus. There are hepatic and renal portal systems. Red blood cells are nucleated and contain haemoglobin. A pair of dark red kidneys made of nephrons excretes urea, so the frog is ureotelic. In males the ureters act as urinogenital ducts; in females the ureters and oviducts open separately into the cloaca.
body.kn: ಕಪ್ಪೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ರಕ್ತಪರಿಚಲನೆ; ಹೃದಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಎರಡು ಹೃತ್ಕರ್ಣ, ಒಂದು ಹೃತ್ಕುಕ್ಷಿ. ಸೈನಸ್ ವೀನೋಸಸ್ ಮತ್ತು ಕೋನಸ್ ಆರ್ಟೀರಿಯೋಸಸ್ ಇವೆ. ಕೆಂಪು ರಕ್ತಕಣಗಳಿಗೆ ಕೋಶಕೇಂದ್ರ ಇದೆ. ಕಪ್ಪೆ ಯೂರಿಯಾ ವಿಸರ್ಜಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: Sinus venosus, conus arteriosus; hepatic and renal portal systems

body.en: The nervous system has a central part (brain and spinal cord), a peripheral part with ten pairs of cranial nerves, and an autonomic part. The brain has a forebrain (olfactory lobes, cerebral hemispheres, diencephalon), a midbrain with a pair of optic lobes, and a hindbrain (cerebellum and medulla oblongata). In males, yellowish testes are attached to the kidneys by the mesorchium; 10–12 vasa efferentia enter the kidneys and open into Bidder's canal, which leads to the urinogenital duct. Females have ovaries and oviducts with no functional connection to the kidneys. A female can lay 2500–3000 ova at a time; fertilisation is external, in water, and the tadpole larva undergoes metamorphosis into the adult.
body.kn: ಕಪ್ಪೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹತ್ತು ಜೊತೆ ಕಪಾಲ ನರಗಳು. ಮಿದುಳು: ಮುಮ್ಮಿದುಳು, ಮಧ್ಯಮಿದುಳು (ದೃಷ್ಟಿ ಹಾಲೆಗಳು), ಹಿಮ್ಮಿದುಳು. ಗಂಡಿನಲ್ಲಿ ವಾಸಾ ಎಫರೆನ್ಷಿಯಾ ಬಿಡ್ಡರ್ ನಾಳಕ್ಕೆ ತೆರೆಯುತ್ತವೆ. ಬಾಹ್ಯ ಫಲೀಕರಣ; ಗೊದಮೊಟ್ಟೆ ರೂಪಾಂತರಗೊಂಡು ಕಪ್ಪೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: Vasa efferentia (10–12) → Bidder's canal → urinogenital duct

steps.en: Testis → vasa efferentia (10–12 in number), which enter the kidney on its side.
Inside the kidney they open into Bidder's canal.
Bidder's canal communicates with the urinogenital duct (ureter), which opens into the cloaca and then outside.

answer.en: Testis → vasa efferentia → Bidder's canal → urinogenital duct → cloaca → outside
